I fixed all four points from the PR #34 review and pushed them as one commit, `de6ccad`. Clippy, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo test` pass locally; CI on the new commit hasn't finished yet.

1. **Missing test (the reviewer's merge blocker):** a new unit test, `analytic_covariance_matches_analytic_signal` in `src/music.rs`, compares the new covariance with the one built from `analytic_signal`. It uses 4 channels of pseudo-random data for every length from 1 to 40, odd and even, and allows a relative difference of 1e-12. To check that it can fail, I briefly doubled the Nyquist bin's weight: the test caught it at N = 2.
2. **Duplicated input checks:** `check_real_samples` now also returns the largest magnitude. `estimate_doa_from_real` calls it instead of keeping its own copy, and the error order is unchanged.
3. **Plan cache:** the doc comment on `real_fft_plan` now says each thread keeps up to 4 plans until it exits. A new test, `real_fft_plan_cache_reuses_and_evicts` in `src/stft.rs`, checks that a cached plan is reused, that the cache holds at most 4, and that the least recently used one is dropped first.
4. **Out-of-date docs:** the function's docs and `CLAUDE.md` no longer say it "calls `estimate_doa`". They now say it works from the covariance directly and doesn't call `estimate_doa`. The docs also note that the data is scaled by an exact power of two, so the covariance isn't rescaled a second time.

# musicrs Rust implementation of MUltiple SIgnal Classification (MUSIC), described by R. O. Schmidt ([paper](http://ieeexplore.ieee.org/xpl/articleDetails.jsp?arnumber=1143830)), for Direction-of-Arrival (DOA) estimation with microphone arrays. It is a port of [pyMUSIC](https://github.com/amjadsaadeh/pyMUSIC), the implementation written for empirical investigations of MUSIC in my master thesis. Pure Rust, no LAPACK. ## Features - Narrowband MUSIC: covariance → noise subspace (Hermitian eigendecomposition via `faer`) → pseudo-spectrum `1 / ‖Eₙᴴ a(θ)‖²` → peak picking. - Multi-source peak picking (circular local maxima, highest first). pyMUSIC's `getSourceAngles` clustered all estimates around the first peak; this is fixed here. - IFB-MUSIC (wideband): per-bin cross-spectral matrices from an STFT, narrowband spectra combined by geometric mean. - FFT-based analytic signal (Hilbert transform) and STFT helpers. ## Usage ```rust use musicrs::MusicEstimator; use nalgebra::DMatrix; // Default: Kinect 4-mic linear array, 720 angle steps over [0, 2π), 16 kHz let estimator = MusicEstimator::default(); // 4 × N real-valued microphone samples, e.g. read from a WAV file let data: DMatrix = /* ... */; // Narrowband DOA of one 1400 Hz source, in radians let angles = estimator.estimate_doa_from_real(&data, 1, 1400.0)?; // Wideband: IFB-MUSIC spectrum over chosen STFT bins (nfft = 160 → 100 Hz bins) let (spectrum, angles) = estimator.ifb_music_spectrum(&data, 160, 1, Some(&[14]))?; ``` Bad input (wrong channel count, NaN, silence, too many sources, an unusable angle grid, …) is returned as a `MusicError`. For other arrays use `MusicEstimator::new(antenna_positions, angle_steps_num, search_interval, sample_rate)` with `[x, y]` positions in metres. If you already have complex (analytic) data, call `estimate_doa` directly. ### Things to keep in mind - A linear array cannot distinguish θ from 360° − θ; restrict `search_interval` to [0, π] if you want a single answer. - IFB-MUSIC only sees frequencies up to Nyquist (`sample_rate / 2`); a tone recorded above Nyquist is aliased and its DOA cannot be recovered from the STFT bins. - Running IFB-MUSIC over *all* bins on a narrowband signal is dominated by noise-only bins; select the bins that carry signal energy. ## Performance vs pyMUSIC and numpy The same calls on the same recordings (1400 Hz, 40°), from the real-valued samples to the result, in three implementations: - **pyMUSIC**, run unmodified; - **numpy (vectorized)**, pyMUSIC's algorithm written the way numpy is meant to be used ([`bench/bench_numpy.py`](bench/bench_numpy.py)): the same analytic signal, `np.linalg.eig` and steering vectors, but in `float64`, with all 720 angles in one array operation, on one thread. Before timing, its spectra are checked against pyMUSIC's (relative difference below 1e-7, same peak); - **musicrs**, single-threaded. **Against pyMUSIC, musicrs is 61× to 2,447× faster, but that is not a Rust-vs-Python result.** Almost all of pyMUSIC's time goes to a Python loop that builds the 720 steering vectors one element at a time in software-emulated `float128`, with `np.matrix` products. That loop costs ~145–165 ms per pseudo-spectrum whatever the recording length, and IFB-MUSIC needs one spectrum per bin. Written idiomatically, the same algorithm in numpy takes milliseconds. **Against vectorized numpy, musicrs is 2.0× to 3.0× faster on narrowband DOA and 3.9× faster on IFB-MUSIC over 80 bins, but 2.1× to 2.3× slower on single-bin IFB-MUSIC.** - *Narrowband* never forms the analytic signals. Their covariance is computed directly from each channel's real FFT (Parseval's theorem), so there is no inverse FFT and no complex N-sample matrix, and the FFT plans are reused between calls. numpy does a complex FFT and an inverse FFT per channel and then a matrix product over all samples. - *IFB-MUSIC over 80 bins* is dominated by the per-bin work of 80 eigendecompositions and 80 spectra. numpy pays Python and call overhead for each bin. - *Single-bin IFB-MUSIC* hasn't been optimised yet. musicrs computes the STFT and the power of every bin, then uses only one of them. It has not been profiled. | Workload | Implementation | n | Mean ± stddev | Median | p5 – p95 | CV | musicrs speedup (mean) | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Narrowband DOA · 1 s recording | pyMUSIC | 200 | 164 ms ± 12.1 ms | 160 ms | 153 ms – 191 ms | 7.4% | 152× | | | numpy (vectorized) | 1000 | 3.28 ms ± 370 µs | 3.2 ms | 2.88 ms – 4.06 ms | 11.3% | 3.03× | | | musicrs | 1000 | 1.08 ms ± 90 µs | 1.07 ms | 982 µs – 1.22 ms | 8.3% | | | Narrowband DOA · 2 s recording | pyMUSIC | 200 | 161 ms ± 8.79 ms | 158 ms | 154 ms – 175 ms | 5.5% | 61× | | | numpy (vectorized) | 1000 | 5.47 ms ± 639 µs | 5.33 ms | 4.88 ms – 6.45 ms | 11.7% | 2.05× | | | musicrs | 1000 | 2.66 ms ± 998 µs | 2.48 ms | 2.24 ms – 3.44 ms | 37.5% | | | IFB-MUSIC, 1 bin · 1 s recording | pyMUSIC | 200 | 146 ms ± 5.88 ms | 144 ms | 141 ms – 161 ms | 4.0% | 124× | | | numpy (vectorized) | 1000 | 552 µs ± 53 µs | 538 µs | 497 µs – 657 µs | 9.6% | 0.47× | | | musicrs | 1000 | 1.17 ms ± 111 µs | 1.16 ms | 1.05 ms – 1.32 ms | 9.5% | | | IFB-MUSIC, 1 bin · 2 s recording | pyMUSIC | 200 | 150 ms ± 5.8 ms | 148 ms | 145 ms – 163 ms | 3.9% | 70× | | | numpy (vectorized) | 1000 | 922 µs ± 166 µs | 869 µs | 792 µs – 1.23 ms | 18.0% | 0.43× | | | musicrs | 1000 | 2.15 ms ± 178 µs | 2.11 ms | 1.95 ms – 2.44 ms | 8.3% | | | IFB-MUSIC, 80 bins · 1 s recording | pyMUSIC | 30 | 11.63 s ± 216 ms | 11.55 s | 11.37 s – 11.92 s | 1.9% | 2,447× | | | numpy (vectorized) | 1000 | 18.7 ms ± 1.35 ms | 18.4 ms | 17.4 ms – 21.5 ms | 7.2% | 3.94× | | | musicrs | 1000 | 4.75 ms ± 1.29 ms | 4.45 ms | 4.15 ms – 5.64 ms | 27.2% | | *musicrs speedup*: the row's mean time over musicrs's; below 1× musicrs is slower. Every call is timed separately (pyMUSIC: 200 calls per case, 30 for 80 bins; numpy and musicrs: 1000) after 3 warm-up calls, the three implementations one after the other on an otherwise idle machine. Machine: Intel N150 (3 cores), Linux, `performance` governor, rustc 1.88, Python 3.10 / numpy 1.23.5 (OpenBLAS, one thread); see [`bench/`](bench/README.md) for the harnesses and how to reproduce, and [`bench/results/`](bench/results/) for the raw samples. ### musicrs over time The same benchmark at three points in musicrs's history, each a separate run on the same machine. Times are mean (median) per call. Separate runs differ by up to ~20 % (see *Run to run* below), so only changes well beyond that mean anything. | Workload | [`b2756f8`](https://github.com/amjadsaadeh/musicrs/commit/b2756f8278c7bf36e28386c87594b274ca8d2b51) | [`4b52605`](https://github.com/amjadsaadeh/musicrs/commit/4b52605f9151899167d8bc147e4d004e8556bfbf) | [`3e2b808`](https://github.com/amjadsaadeh/musicrs/commit/3e2b8081e300fc4e8b8a06d40613dc43ad410385) | numpy (vectorized), latest run | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Narrowband DOA · 1 s | 5.63 ms (5.41 ms) | 6.29 ms (6.04 ms) | **1.08 ms (1.07 ms)** | 3.28 ms | | Narrowband DOA · 2 s | 11.7 ms (11.5 ms) | 13.4 ms (13.0 ms) | **2.66 ms (2.48 ms)** | 5.47 ms | | IFB-MUSIC, 1 bin · 1 s | 757 µs (770 µs) | 1.12 ms (1.10 ms) | 1.17 ms (1.16 ms) | 552 µs | | IFB-MUSIC, 1 bin · 2 s | 1.24 ms (1.22 ms) | 2.48 ms (2.50 ms) | 2.15 ms (2.11 ms) | 922 µs | | IFB-MUSIC, 80 bins · 1 s | 14.7 ms (14.5 ms) | 5.43 ms (5.46 ms) | 4.75 ms (4.45 ms) | 18.7 ms | - [`b2756f8`](https://github.com/amjadsaadeh/musicrs/commit/b2756f8278c7bf36e28386c87594b274ca8d2b51): the first benchmark. Its results were committed with that commit; which code they were measured on was not recorded. - [`4b52605`](https://github.com/amjadsaadeh/musicrs/commit/4b52605f9151899167d8bc147e4d004e8556bfbf): `main` after #23–#29. Among other changes, IFB-MUSIC builds its cross-spectral matrices one bin at a time (#23) and the channels share one FFT planner (#26). Over 80 bins IFB-MUSIC became ~3× faster, while single-bin IFB-MUSIC became 1.5–2× slower. That slowdown has not been profiled. - [`3e2b808`](https://github.com/amjadsaadeh/musicrs/commit/3e2b8081e300fc4e8b8a06d40613dc43ad410385): narrowband DOA computes the covariance from real FFTs (#34), and `spectrum` no longer allocates per angle. Narrowband DOA is 5–6× faster than at [`4b52605`](https://github.com/amjadsaadeh/musicrs/commit/4b52605f9151899167d8bc147e4d004e8556bfbf). The raw samples of each run are in the repository, e.g. `git show 14e54d6:bench/results/musicrs.csv` (run on [`4b52605`](https://github.com/amjadsaadeh/musicrs/commit/4b52605f9151899167d8bc147e4d004e8556bfbf)) and `git show ed4faa7:bench/results/musicrs.csv` (run on [`3e2b808`](https://github.com/amjadsaadeh/musicrs/commit/3e2b8081e300fc4e8b8a06d40613dc43ad410385)); `bench/results/environment.txt` in the same commit records the machine and the musicrs commit. ### Distribution of the timings - **Not normal.** Shapiro-Wilk rejects normality for every case, on t and on log t (p < 0.001; p ≈ 0.03 for pyMUSIC over 80 bins, which has only 30 calls). Every distribution is right-skewed (skew 0.5 to 4.8, and 10 to 16 for the two musicrs cases below): a sharp edge near the fastest call and a tail of slower ones, the shape of interference that can only add time. A log-normal fits better than a normal in every case, but none is log-normal either. - **Scheduling moves the mean by a few percent.** The mean is at most 7.3 % above the median, and the outliers (calls slower than median + 3 robust sigmas) raise the mean by at most 6.0 % (*tail excess*). Both maxima come from musicrs on narrowband DOA (2 s recording) and IFB-MUSIC over 80 bins. Each has a small group of calls at twice the median or more (the last histogram bin), which no other case has. For these two, the median is the better single number. Mean and median give the same ratios to within 7 %. Because the distributions are skewed, ± stddev overstates the spread below the mean; the p5 – p95 column shows the real range. - **Slow calls come in runs.** Lag-1 autocorrelation is 0.2 to 0.7, so neighbouring calls are alike. Isolated preemptions would hit calls independently; runs point to slower changes in machine state (CPU frequency, caches, the core the process runs on). - **Run to run**, numpy's means moved by up to 9 % and pyMUSIC's by up to 3 % against a run the day before, and a shorter musicrs run an hour earlier gave means up to 9 % lower. Read the numbers as about ± 20 %. The ratios between musicrs and numpy (2× to 4×) are larger than that, and the ratios to pyMUSIC far larger.

Benchmark against a vectorized numpy baseline
## Summary

The README benchmark compared musicrs only against pyMUSIC as published. Profiling shows almost all of pyMUSIC's time goes to a per-angle Python loop that builds 720 `float128` steering vectors with `np.matrix`. So the "14× to 784× faster" headline measured how pyMUSIC is written, not Rust vs Python.

This PR:

- **Adds `bench/bench_numpy.py`.** It runs pyMUSIC's algorithm written idiomatically in numpy: the same analytic signal, `np.linalg.eig`, steering vectors and peak, in `float64`, with all angles in one array operation, one BLAS thread and no caching between calls. Before timing each case it checks its result against pyMUSIC's on the same recording; every case matched to a relative difference below 1e-7.
- **Re-runs all three implementations** on the current code, one after another. The old musicrs results predated #23 and #26. `environment.txt` now records the musicrs commit.
- **Updates `bench/analyze.py`** for three implementations: a speedup column against each baseline, a dot plot on a log time axis (the linear bars would make numpy and musicrs invisible next to 11.5 s), and three-column histograms.
- **Rewrites the README section and `bench/README.md`.**
- **Fixes `bench_pymusic.py`:** with `BENCH_SCALE` set, the second recording of a workload was scaled twice. Full runs were not affected.

## Results

| Workload | pyMUSIC | numpy (vectorized) | musicrs | musicrs vs numpy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Narrowband · 1 s | 160 ms | 3.03 ms | 6.29 ms | 2.1× slower |
| Narrowband · 2 s | 158 ms | 5.02 ms | 13.4 ms | 2.7× slower |
| IFB, 1 bin · 1 s | 144 ms | 512 µs | 1.12 ms | 2.2× slower |
| IFB, 1 bin · 2 s | 149 ms | 855 µs | 2.48 ms | 2.9× slower |
| IFB, 80 bins · 1 s | 11.56 s | 18.8 ms | 5.43 ms | 3.5× faster |

Speeding up musicrs's narrowband and single-bin path (likely the Hilbert transform/STFT and the covariance, not yet profiled) is left for a separate PR.

## Test plan

- [x] `bench_numpy.py` parity check against pyMUSIC passes for every case
- [x] Full runs of all three harnesses; `analyze.py` regenerates `summary.{csv,md}` and the charts
- [x] Charts rendered and checked in light and dark mode

def load_pymusic():
    """pyMUSIC with the pySoundToolbox shim of bench_pymusic.py, for the parity check only."""
    with open(os.path.join(toolbox_dir, "pySoundToolbox.py")) as f:
        src = f.read()
    start = src.index("def genAnalyticSignal")
    end = src.index("\nclass ", start)
    toolbox_mod = types.ModuleType("pySoundToolbox.pySoundToolbox")
    toolbox_mod.np = np
    exec(src[start:end].replace("n / 2", "n // 2"), toolbox_mod.__dict__)
    pkg = types.ModuleType("pySoundToolbox")
    pkg.pySoundToolbox = toolbox_mod
    sys.modules["pySoundToolbox"] = pkg
    sys.modules["pySoundToolbox.pySoundToolbox"] = toolbox_mod
    sys.path.insert(0, pymusic_dir)
    import pyMUSIC

    return pyMUSIC


def check_parity(pymusic, name, data):
    """Same result as pyMUSIC on this recording, or the timings would not be comparable."""
    est = pymusic.MUSICEst()
    if name == "narrowband":
        ref, got = est.getSourceAngles(data, 1, FREQ), source_angles(data, 1, FREQ)
        # The linear array cannot tell theta from 2 pi - theta: both peaks are equal up to
        # rounding, so either may come first
        mirror = np.mod(2 * np.pi - got, 2 * np.pi)
        assert np.allclose(ref, got) or np.allclose(ref, mirror), \
            f"{name}: pyMUSIC {np.degrees(ref)}, numpy {np.degrees(got)}"
        # The angle alone could agree by chance: compare the spectra too
        a = analytic_signal(data)
        nm = est.getNoiseMat(np.matrix(a @ a.conj().T / data.shape[1]), 1)
        ref_spec, _ = est.getSpectrum(nm, FREQ)
        got_spec, _ = spectrum(noise_mat(a @ a.conj().T / data.shape[1], 1), FREQ)
    else:
        bins = BINS[name]
        ref_spec, _ = pymusic.IFBMUSICSpectrum(data, est.antennaPositions, NFFT, bins=bins)
        got_spec, _ = ifb_music_spectrum(data, NFFT, bins)
    rel = float(np.max(np.abs(got_spec / ref_spec - 1)))
    # pyMUSIC's peak is also a peak here (ties between mirror angles may break either way)
    assert rel < 1e-6 and got_spec[np.argmax(ref_spec)] >= got_spec.max() * (1 - 1e-6), \
        f"{name}: rel. diff {rel}"
    return rel


BINS = {"ifb_one_bin": [FREQ * NFFT // SAMPLE_RATE], "ifb_all_bins": list(range(1, NFFT // 2 + 1))}

# Same workloads, recordings and sample counts as examples/bench_pymusic.rs
WORKLOADS = [
    ("narrowband", lambda d: source_angles(d, 1, FREQ), ("1.0", "2.0"), 1000),
    ("ifb_one_bin", lambda d: ifb_music_spectrum(d, NFFT, BINS["ifb_one_bin"]), ("1.0", "2.0"), 1000),
    ("ifb_all_bins", lambda d: ifb_music_spectrum(d, NFFT, BINS["ifb_all_bins"]), ("1.0",), 1000),
]


def main():
    pymusic = load_pymusic()
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out_path) or ".", exist_ok=True)
    with open(out_path, "w") as out:

        for name, run, durations, samples in WORKLOADS:
            for duration in durations:
                data = read_wav_4ch(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, f"single-source_{FREQ}Hz_40deg_{duration}s.wav"))
                rel = check_parity(pymusic, name, data)
                n = max(5, round(samples * SCALE))
                for _ in range(WARMUP):

                for i in range(n):

                    out.write(f"numpy,{name},{duration},{i},{dt / 1e9!r}\n")
                out.flush()
                print(f"numpy {name} {duration}s: {n} samples (max rel. diff to pyMUSIC {rel:.1e})",
                      file=sys.stderr)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    eigenvectors sorted by |eigenvalue|, the same steering vectors exp(-j 2 pi f tau) and the
    same peak (the first maximum of the spectrum);
  * but in float64, with the steering vectors of all angles built in one array operation

  * the IFB geometric mean is accumulated as a sum of logarithms, as in musicrs.

    h[n // 2] = 1

"""Time a vectorized numpy implementation of pyMUSIC's algorithm and write every sample to a CSV.

Usage (from the repo root; same environment as bench/bench_pymusic.py):

    uv run --python 3.10 --with 'numpy==1.23.5' python -I bench/bench_numpy.py \
        /path/to/pyMUSIC /path/to/pySoundToolbox bench/results/numpy.csv

pyMUSIC spends almost all of its time in a Python loop over the 720 angles that builds every
steering vector element by element in float128 with np.matrix. Timing only that measures how
pyMUSIC is written, not what Python with numpy can do. This script runs the same algorithm
written the way numpy is meant to be used, as the baseline musicrs should be measured against:

  * the same analytic signal (pySoundToolbox.genAnalyticSignal: FFT, one-sided spectrum, IFFT,
    conjugate), the same covariance and cross-spectral matrices, the same np.linalg.eig with
    eigenvectors sorted by |eigenvalue|, the same steering vectors exp(-j 2 pi f tau) and the
    same peak (the first maximum of the spectrum);
  * but in float64, with the steering vectors of all angles built in one array operation
    every call (nothing is cached between calls), all channels transformed at once, and
    1 / ||En^H a||^2 instead of a^H En En^H a (equal, as En En^H is Hermitian);
  * the IFB geometric mean is accumulated as a sum of logarithms, as in musicrs.

numpy is limited to one thread (musicrs is single-threaded). Before timing, every workload is
checked against pyMUSIC itself on the same recording: same peak angle, spectrum within a
relative 1e-6 (narrowband: also the covariance, built from pySoundToolbox's analytic signal). The workloads, sample counts and CSV format mirror bench_pymusic.py and
examples/bench_pymusic.rs; see bench/README.md.
"""

import os

# Before numpy is imported: one BLAS/LAPACK thread, as musicrs
for var in ("OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS", "OMP_NUM_THREADS", "MKL_NUM_THREADS"):
    os.environ[var] = "1"

import sys  # noqa: E402
import time  # noqa: E402
import types  # noqa: E402
import wave  # noqa: E402

import numpy as np  # noqa: E402

pymusic_dir, toolbox_dir, out_path = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
SCALE = float(os.environ.get("BENCH_SCALE", "1"))

DATA_DIR = "tests/data/single-source"
NFFT = 160
FREQ = 1400
WARMUP = 3
SAMPLE_RATE = 16000
SPEED_OF_SOUND = 343.2  # m/s, as pyMUSIC
# pyMUSIC's default MUSICEst: Kinect array, 720 angles over [0, 2 pi)
MIC_POSITIONS = np.array([[0.113, -0.036, -0.076, -0.113], [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]])
ANGLE_STEPS = 720


def angle_grid():
    return np.arange(0, 2 * np.pi, 2 * np.pi / ANGLE_STEPS)


def spectrum(noise_mat, frequency):
    """MUSIC pseudo-spectrum over the angle grid, as MUSICEst.getSpectrum (cov mode)."""
    angles = angle_grid()
    delays = MIC_POSITIONS.T @ np.vstack([np.cos(angles), np.sin(angles)]) / SPEED_OF_SOUND
    steering = np.exp(-2j * np.pi * frequency * delays)  # (mics, angles)
    proj = noise_mat.conj().T @ steering  # (noise dims, angles)
    return 1.0 / np.einsum("ij,ij->j", proj.conj(), proj).real, angles


def noise_mat(cov, n_sources):
    """As MUSICEst.getNoiseMat: np.linalg.eig, eigenvectors of the smallest |eigenvalues|."""
    values, vectors = np.linalg.eig(cov)
    return vectors[:, np.argsort(np.abs(values), kind="stable")[: cov.shape[0] - n_sources]]


def analytic_signal(data):
    """pySoundToolbox.genAnalyticSignal, for all channels (rows) at once."""
    n = data.shape[1]
    h = np.zeros(n)
    h[0] = 1
    h[n // 2] = 1
    h[1 : n // 2] = 2
    return np.fft.ifft(np.fft.fft(data, axis=1) * h, axis=1)


def covariance(data):
    """As MUSICEst.getSourceAngles: covariance of the channels' analytic signals."""
    a = analytic_signal(data)

"""Time a vectorized numpy implementation of pyMUSIC's algorithm and write every sample to a CSV.

Usage (from the repo root; same environment as bench/bench_pymusic.py):

    uv run --python 3.10 --with 'numpy==1.23.5' python -I bench/bench_numpy.py \
        /path/to/pyMUSIC /path/to/pySoundToolbox bench/results/numpy.csv

pyMUSIC spends almost all of its time in a Python loop over the 720 angles that builds every
steering vector element by element in float128 with np.matrix. Timing only that measures how
pyMUSIC is written, not what Python with numpy can do. This script runs the same algorithm
written the way numpy is meant to be used, as the baseline musicrs should be measured against:

  * the same analytic signal (pySoundToolbox.genAnalyticSignal: FFT, one-sided spectrum, IFFT,
    conjugate), the same covariance and cross-spectral matrices, the same np.linalg.eig with
    eigenvectors sorted by |eigenvalue|, the same steering vectors exp(-j 2 pi f tau) and the
    same peak (the first maximum of the spectrum);
  * but in float64, with the steering vectors of all angles built in one array operation
    every call (nothing is cached between calls), all channels transformed at once, and
    1 / ||En^H a||^2 instead of a^H En En^H a (equal, as En En^H is Hermitian);
  * the IFB geometric mean is accumulated as a sum of logarithms, as in musicrs.

numpy is limited to one thread (musicrs is single-threaded). Before timing, every workload is
checked against pyMUSIC itself on the same recording: same peak angle, spectrum within a
relative 1e-6 (narrowband: also the covariance, built from pySoundToolbox's analytic signal). The workloads, sample counts and CSV format mirror bench_pymusic.py and
examples/bench_pymusic.rs; see bench/README.md.
"""

import os

# Before numpy is imported: one BLAS/LAPACK thread, as musicrs
for var in ("OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS", "OMP_NUM_THREADS", "MKL_NUM_THREADS"):
    os.environ[var] = "1"

import time  # noqa: E402
import types  # noqa: E402
import wave  # noqa: E402

import numpy as np  # noqa: E402

pymusic_dir, toolbox_dir, out_path = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
SCALE = float(os.environ.get("BENCH_SCALE", "1"))

DATA_DIR = "tests/data/single-source"
NFFT = 160
FREQ = 1400
WARMUP = 3
SAMPLE_RATE = 16000
SPEED_OF_SOUND = 343.2  # m/s, as pyMUSIC
# pyMUSIC's default MUSICEst: Kinect array, 720 angles over [0, 2 pi)
MIC_POSITIONS = np.array([[0.113, -0.036, -0.076, -0.113], [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]])
ANGLE_STEPS = 720


def angle_grid():
    return np.arange(0, 2 * np.pi, 2 * np.pi / ANGLE_STEPS)


def spectrum(noise_mat, frequency):
    """MUSIC pseudo-spectrum over the angle grid, as MUSICEst.getSpectrum (cov mode)."""
    angles = angle_grid()
    delays = MIC_POSITIONS.T @ np.vstack([np.cos(angles), np.sin(angles)]) / SPEED_OF_SOUND
    steering = np.exp(-2j * np.pi * frequency * delays)  # (mics, angles)
    proj = noise_mat.conj().T @ steering  # (noise dims, angles)
    return 1.0 / np.einsum("ij,ij->j", proj.conj(), proj).real, angles


def noise_mat(cov, n_sources):
    """As MUSICEst.getNoiseMat: np.linalg.eig, eigenvectors of the smallest |eigenvalues|."""
    values, vectors = np.linalg.eig(cov)
    return vectors[:, np.argsort(np.abs(values), kind="stable")[: cov.shape[0] - n_sources]]


def analytic_signal(data):
    """pySoundToolbox.genAnalyticSignal, for all channels (rows) at once."""
    n = data.shape[1]
    h = np.zeros(n)
    h[0] = 1
    h[n // 2] = 1
    h[1 : n // 2] = 2
    return np.fft.ifft(np.fft.fft(data, axis=1) * h, axis=1).conj()


def covariance(data):
    """As MUSICEst.getSourceAngles: covariance of the channels' analytic signals."""
    a = analytic_signal(data)
    return a @ a.conj().T / data.shape[1]


def source_angles(data, n_sources, frequency):
    """As MUSICEst.getSourceAngles for one source: the angle of the first maximum."""
    spec, angles = spectrum(noise_mat(covariance(data), n_sources), frequency)
    return angles[np.argsort(-spec, kind="stable")[:n_sources]]


def ifb_music_spectrum(data, nfft, bins, n_sources=1):
    """As pyMUSIC.IFBMUSICSpectrum: non-overlapping rectangular STFT, geometric mean of bins."""
    n_windows = data.shape[1] // nfft
    frames = data[:, : n_windows * nfft].reshape(data.shape[0], n_windows, nfft)
    stft = np.fft.rfft(frames, axis=2)  # (mics, windows, bins)
    freqs = np.fft.rfftfreq(nfft, 1 / SAMPLE_RATE)
    log_sum = np.zeros(ANGLE_STEPS)
    for b in bins:
        x = stft[:, :, b]

        # The linear array cannot tell theta from 2 pi - theta: both peaks are equal up to

        # The angle alone could agree by chance (and accepts the mirror angle): compare the
        # covariance and the spectrum too. The reference covariance is built as
        # getSourceAngles builds it, from pySoundToolbox's genAnalyticSignal, so a mistake in
        # analytic_signal (a missing conjugate would mirror the spectrum) cannot pass.
        gen = sys.modules["pySoundToolbox.pySoundToolbox"].genAnalyticSignal
        a = np.array([gen(row) for row in data])
        ref_cov = a @ a.conj().T / data.shape[1]
        got_cov = covariance(data)
        cov_rel = float(np.max(np.abs(got_cov - ref_cov)) / np.max(np.abs(ref_cov)))
        assert cov_rel < 1e-12, f"{name}: covariance rel. diff {cov_rel}"
        ref_spec, _ = est.getSpectrum(est.getNoiseMat(np.matrix(ref_cov), 1), FREQ)
        got_spec, _ = spectrum(noise_mat(got_cov, 1), FREQ)
    else:
        bins = BINS[name]
        ref_spec, _ = pymusic.IFBMUSICSpectrum(data, est.antennaPositions, NFFT, bins=bins)
        got_spec, _ = ifb_music_spectrum(data, NFFT, bins)

    # pyMUSIC's peak is also a peak here (ties between mirror angles may break either way)
    assert rel < 1e-6 and got_spec[np.argmax(ref_spec)] >= got_spec.max() * (1 - 1e-6), \
        f"{name}: rel. diff {rel}"
    return rel

    ("narrowband", lambda d: source_angles(d, 1, FREQ), ("1.0", "2.0"), 1000),
    ("ifb_one_bin", lambda d: ifb_music_spectrum(d, NFFT, BINS["ifb_one_bin"]), ("1.0", "2.0"), 1000),
    ("ifb_all_bins", lambda d: ifb_music_spectrum(d, NFFT, BINS["ifb_all_bins"]), ("1.0",), 1000),
]


def main():
    pymusic = load_pymusic()
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out_path) or ".", exist_ok=True)
    with open(out_path, "w") as out:
        out.write("implementation,workload,recording_s,iteration,seconds\n")
        for name, run, durations, samples in WORKLOADS:

                data = read_wav_4ch(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, f"single-source_{FREQ}Hz_40deg_{duration}s.wav"))
                rel = check_parity(pymusic, name, data)
                n = max(5, round(samples * SCALE))
